title: Critical Auth0 AD/LDAP Connector Flaw Lets Attackers Execute Stored XSS in Admin Browsers
content_md: Okta has released security updates for three high-severity vulnerabilities affecting the Auth0 AD/LDAP Connector and Okta Access Gateway, including a critical stored cross-site scripting flaw that could execute attacker-controlled code in an administrator’s browser. The vulnerabilities, disclosed on September 8, 2026, include stored XSS, authorization bypass, and SQL injection issues. Organizations using the affected identity infrastructure should prioritize remediation, especially where Access Gateway secures sensitive enterprise applications or privileged IT personnel administer Auth0 directory connectors. Critical Auth0 AD/LDAP Connector Flaw The most severe vulnerability, CVE-2026-85982 , impacts the Auth0 AD/LDAP Connector and carries a CVSS v3 score of 9.0. The flaw stems from improper HTML encoding of directory search-result data and updater log content displayed in the connector’s administrative interface. An attacker with authenticated access to a connected directory could exploit the issue by modifying user-editable directory attributes to include malicious JavaScript. A low-privileged local user with access to the system hosting the connector could also potentially inject malicious content into updater logs or associated local data fields. The malicious payload is stored until an administrator opens the affected directory search results or updater logs through the Auth0 AD/LDAP Connector Admin Panel.
